subject.title: Telegram should default to allowlist mode with owner ID

question: Should Telegram retain pairing as the fresh-install default and optionally flip after verified first-owner approval, or should verified Telegram setup immediately persist allowlist mode with the captured owner ID?
rationale: Both paths improve the reported exposure but differ in first-run accessibility, cross-channel policy consistency, persisted-config migration, and the security contract for identifying the initial owner.

options.title: Verified setup writes allowlist
options.body: Use a short one-time challenge token during fresh Telegram setup, then persist the matching numeric sender ID in allowFrom and set dmPolicy to allowlist without changing existing explicit pairing configs.

options.title: Retain pairing then auto-flip
options.body: Keep pairing for first contact and switch only after the first approved owner is established, respecting any explicit channel policy.

options.title: Keep current model and improve guidance
options.body: Retain pairing as the default and make the existing manual numeric allowlist path more visible in setup and security documentation.

recommendation.title: Verified setup writes allowlist
recommendation.body: Use a short one-time challenge token during fresh Telegram setup, then persist the matching numeric sender ID in allowFrom and set dmPolicy to allowlist without changing existing explicit pairing configs.

likelyOwner.reason: Current Telegram policy and setup work spans runtime, documentation, and configuration decisions associated with this area.
